description: Figure 9 is a composite of two CALPHAD phase-fraction diagrams plus one SEM micrograph. (a) and (b) both plot "Amount of all phases [mol]" (y-axis, 0.00-1.10) against "Temperature [°C]" (x-axis, 0-1300 in 100° ticks). (a) [legend: BCC_A2 dark, FCC_A1 red, KAPPA_E21 green] is for 9Al-10Mn-0.4: BCC_A2 dominates at ~0.87-0.92 mol below ~700 °C then falls to a ~0.51 minimum at 800 °C; FCC_A1 is near zero to ~700 °C, rises steeply to ~0.49 mol at 800 °C and declines to ~0.28 mol at 1300 °C; KAPPA_E21 holds ~0.10 mol (200-700 °C) and vanishes near 850 °C. (b) [legend order/colours: FCC_A1 blue, BCC_A2 red, KAPPA_E21 green] is for 9Al-10Mn-1C: BCC_A2 holds ~0.80 mol to ~650 °C, collapses near 800 °C, then rises to ~0.22 mol at 1300 °C; FCC_A1 climbs to ~1.00 mol at ~1000 °C then decreases; KAPPA_E21 ~0.20 mol below 600 °C, zero at ~950 °C. The uncaptioned third panel is a grey SEM micrograph (20 µm scale bar) with equiaxed grains, dark grain-boundary lines and a horizontal crack/band. The curves quantify the thermodynamic gradient in austenite stability that the text ties to tempering-induced austenite decomposition.

observations.observation: (a) plots 'Amount of all phases [mol]' (y-axis, 0.00-1.10) versus 'Temperature [°C]' (x-axis, 0-1300 in 100° steps) with legend entries BCC_A2, FCC_A1 and KAPPA_E21.
In (a) the BCC_A2 curve is the largest at low temperature (~0.87-0.92 mol, plateau from ~200 to ~700 °C) and drops steeply to a minimum of about 0.51 mol at 800 °C before rising again.
In (a) the FCC_A1 curve is near zero until ~700 °C, rises steeply to a maximum of ~0.49 mol at 800 °C, then declines toward ~0.28 mol at 1300 °C.
In (a) KAPPA_E21 stays near 0.10 mol between roughly 200 and 700 °C and falls to zero at about 850 °C.
(b) uses the same axis format for the higher-carbon alloy, with legend listed as FCC_A1, BCC_A2 and KAPPA_E21 and different line colours from (a) (FCC_A1 blue, BCC_A2 red, KAPPA_E21 green).
In (b) the BCC_A2 curve holds ~0.80 mol from 0 to ~650 °C, collapses to near zero around 800 °C, stays near zero until ~1050 °C, then rises to ~0.22 mol at 1300 °C.
In (b) the FCC_A1 curve rises from zero at ~700 °C to a peak of ~1.00 mol at ~1000 °C and then decreases to ~0.78 mol at 1300 °C.
In (b) KAPPA_E21 holds ~0.20 mol below ~600 °C, rises slightly above 0.20 mol near 650 °C, and falls to zero at ~950 °C.
The third, uncaptioned panel is a grey SEM micrograph with a 20 µm scale bar showing equiaxed grains, dark grain-boundary lines and a prominent horizontal crack/band across the centre.
The caption states Fig. 9 gives examples of thermodynamic gradients for austenite stability from phase volume fraction diagrams, (a) for 9Al-10Mn-0.4 and (b) for 9Al-10Mn-1C.
The citing text states that in Fig. 9(a) the austenite fraction along the red line does not decrease at 800 °C compared to 1150 °C.
The citing text reports a drop of γ (austenite) volume fraction from 1150 °C to 600 °C in Fig. 9(a) and a γ fraction gradient in 9Al-10Mn-1C at 600 °C and 800 °C in Fig. 9(b).

subfigures.description: Phase volume fraction diagram for 9Al-10Mn-0.4: 'Amount of all phases [mol]' (0.00-1.10) vs 'Temperature [°C]' (0-1300). Curves BCC_A2 (dark), FCC_A1 (red) and KAPPA_E21 (green); BCC_A2 plateau ~0.87-0.92 mol then steep drop to ~0.51 at 800 °C, FCC_A1 rising to ~0.49 mol at 800 °C, KAPPA_E21 ~0.10 mol removed near 850 °C.

Phase volume fraction diagram for 9Al-10Mn-1C, same axes. Legend FCC_A1 (blue), BCC_A2 (red), KAPPA_E21 (green). BCC_A2 ~0.80 mol to ~650 °C then collapse; FCC_A1 rises to ~1.00 mol at ~1000 °C; KAPPA_E21 ~0.20 mol below 600 °C and zero by ~950 °C.

Grey SEM micrograph with a 20 µm scale bar showing equiaxed grains separated by dark grain-boundary lines, scattered small dark particles, and a prominent horizontal crack/band crossing the centre. Panel label not visible.
